numerical_characteristics.magnitude: vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds); example rho=1 m, z=1e8 m gives theta 0 before fix and 1e-8 rad after
category_specific_evidence: Passages describe a numerical-precision bug in the fast-path CylindricalRepresentation to PhysicsSphericalRepresentation conversion for vectors very close to the Z axis (within milliarcseconds).
Root cause per PR body: np.arccos() used instead of np.arctan2() for theta; diff changes theta=np.arccos(self.z / r) to theta=np.arctan2(self.rho, self.z).
Before the fix, CylindricalRepresentation(1*u.m, 0*u.deg, 1e8*u.m).represent_as(PhysicsSphericalRepresentation).theta gives <Angle 0. rad>; after the fix it gives <Angle 1.e-08 rad>.

Added regression test test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta uses rho=1 m, phi=10 deg, z=1e8 m and checks r, phi and theta with assert_allclose against 1e8 m, 10 deg and 1e-8 rad; the tolerance arguments are not stated in the passage.
The changelog entry describes the same bug as a numerical-precision bug for vectors within milliarcseconds of the Z axis.
reproduction_risks: No dtype is stated in any passage; the dtype the defect depends on is not given.
No precision (such as float32 versus float64) is stated in the passages.

No tolerance is stated for separating correct from incorrect answers; assert_allclose is used with unspecified default or explicit tolerances, so a 1-ULP-level defect's visibility at a default tolerance cannot be established from the passages.
The arccos(z/r) form loses precision for small angles because z/r rounds to 1, so the reproduction needs large z relative to rho.
The numpy version is not stated in the passages.
